items.title: A 40-year-old, self-built Dutch POS with a large installed base
items.summary: Vendit has offered retail automation since 1986, develops its software entirely in-house with about 40 colleagues, and claims 12,000+ users across 25+ branches (other pages say 10,000+ users and 40 branches).
items.implication: The installed base is the asset: retention, migration quality and branch depth matter more than feature breadth. Treat user counts as vendor claims with inconsistent rounding.

items.title: Three packages and an all-in monthly fee
items.summary: Vendit sells POS, Premium and Enterprise packages; POS is listed from EUR 119/month on the pricing page and from EUR 129/month on the kassasysteem page, Premium from EUR 199, Enterprise on request, webshop from EUR 299. The fee includes cloud hosting, updates, support, and the turnkey workplace (hardware, setup, migration, training) is positioned as part of the offer.
items.implication: Packaging maps directly to segments (starter, growing multi-store, chain); upgrade paths between packages are the main expansion lever.

items.title: Branch depth is the differentiator in bike and jewellery retail
items.summary: Vendit says all national bike manufacturers and wholesalers are connected, enabling ordering, supplier stock checks and booking in with frame and DPC numbers; it offers workshop functions, and in July 2026 partnered with the Federatie Goud en Zilver for jewellers, citing gemstone specifications, serial numbers and repair orders.
items.implication: Supplier connectivity and repair management are hard for generic POS vendors to copy; they justify the workshop and supplier bricks.

items.title: Franchise formulas and RSOs are a distinct segment
items.summary: Vendit markets a filiaal solution for retail service organisations with central price, promotion and assortment publication, joint purchasing and purchase-price formulas; the KW Groep (serving Blokker entrepreneurs) is a named reference.
items.implication: RSOs buy for many stores at once and need head-office tooling; model them separately from single-store owners.

items.title: Marketplaces via EffectConnect, shipping via DeliveryMatch
items.summary: Vendit's marketplace module publishes stock, lead time, prices and content to bol, Amazon, VidaXL and Beslist via EffectConnect, imports orders with customer and payment data, and lets users print labels via DeliveryMatch; Vendit states more than 30% of European e-commerce purchases happen on marketplaces (vendor claim, source not given).
items.implication: Sibling integrations make omnichannel selling credible for small retailers without their own webshop; sync latency becomes a key quality metric.

items.title: Vendit is a founding brand of the Katapull group
items.summary: Katapull was formed in March 2025 by bundling Logic4, DeliveryMatch, EffectConnect, Highbiza and Vendit; Returnista was acquired in February 2026 and Picqer in October 2026. Katapull lists Vendit, Logic4, Highbiza, Returnista, EffectConnect, DeliveryMatch, Transus and Picqer as labels of its Commerce Hub, with Vendit and DeliveryMatch sharing an address in Rotterdam.
items.implication: Group membership gives Vendit integration partners and an upgrade path (Logic4) but also raises portfolio-overlap questions to be resolved in strategy.

items.title: Sibling integrations documented on Vendit partner pages
items.summary: Vendit's partner pages state that Highbiza and Transus are linked ("gekoppeld") with the Vendit System and list Logic4 (ERP), DeliveryMatch (shipping) and Returnista (returns) as Katapull partners; Sendcloud, Transsmart, Picqer, Exact/AFAS, CCV, Worldline and Givacard also appear.
items.implication: Evidence for Highbiza, Transus, EffectConnect and DeliveryMatch integration is explicit; Returnista and Logic4 integration depth is not documented and is modeled as an assumption.

items.title: Real-time stock is the core promise
items.summary: Vendit frames stock management around "never sell no again": every sale, return and reservation updates stock instantly in store and webshop, min/max replenishment creates the daily order list, and stock can be moved between branches.
items.implication: Stock accuracy is the hinge KPI for owners, associates and shoppers alike.

items.title: Retailers steer on a standard dashboard
items.summary: The online dashboard compares turnover, margin, discount, number of transactions, items sold, average transaction value and items per transaction with a previous period; reports include top/flop 100, turnover speed, stock valuation and negative margin. TSM Coatings says it steers on the dashboard daily.
items.implication: These measures are the vocabulary of the owner and chain KPI pyramids.

items.title: Service as part of the product
items.summary: Vendit runs a helpdesk Monday to Saturday, offers remote support via TeamViewer and includes online help and updates in the subscription.
items.implication: Saturday support matters for retailers; support load is an early churn signal.

items.title: Competition ranges from global cloud POS to branch specialists
items.summary: Lightspeed reported FY2025 revenue of USD 1,076.8 million; MplusKASSA (since 1985) claims 6,000+ customers and 16k+ locations across hospitality and retail; branch specialists such as CycleSoftware and Wilmar target bike shops.
items.implication: Vendit competes on branch depth, Dutch service and the all-in package rather than global scale.

items.title: Loyalty and gift cards drive repeat visits
items.summary: Vendit supports customer cards with unique barcodes, value cheques and own gift cards via Givacard; a partner quote cites that gift card holders spend about 61% more (partner claim, not independently sourced).
items.implication: Loyalty supports sales on name, which feeds repairs, history and marketing; treat spend uplift as unverified.
